summary.text: A 27-year-old man presented with progressive dysphonia for four years. During this period, several drug treatments, including antibiotics and systemic and inhaled corticosteroids, were unsuccessful, and he refused a biopsy. After further deterioration of the vocal quality he came to the authors' service. Videolaryngoscopy showed diffuse infiltration of the glottic and supraglottic regions with signs of chronic laryngitis, and there were no alterations in the cervical ganglionary chains. The discussion states that he was immunocompetent and had no diagnosis of autoimmune disease.

Computed tomography of the cervical region in previous examinations showed diffuse mucosal thickening of the larynx and cervical tracheal segment with obliteration of the paraglottic and pre-epiglottic fat planes, and laboratory tests showed no alterations. Biopsy at direct laryngoscopy showed amyloidosis with lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate in the right vocal fold, and immunohistochemistry was compatible with MALT lymphoma. The myelogram showed an increased erythrocyte series, and PET-CT showed slight asymmetric radioconcentration with a grade 3 Deauville score.

He was treated with eighteen radiotherapy sessions and showed voice improvement. The authors conclude that the patient, with MALT lymphoma and amyloidosis in the larynx, showed a favorable outcome after radiotherapy treatment.
